questions.title: Question 1: Data structures (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) State what a data structure is and why Program = Algorithm + Data Structure. (b) Classify an `int`, an array, a linked list, a stack and a tree as primitive or non-primitive, linear or non-linear, static or dynamic where that applies. (c) Start with an empty array structure of capacity 8: add 40, add 10, add 30, insert 25 at index 1, delete index 0, modify index 2 to 99, sort. Show the contents after each. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: A data structure is a way of organising data in a computer's memory; it provides a framework for manipulating the data. An algorithm alone is not enough because programs manipulate data, and the choice of structure determines the algorithm's performance. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `int`: primitive. Array: non-primitive, linear, static. Linked list: non-primitive, linear, dynamic. Stack: non-primitive, linear (static or dynamic by implementation). Tree: non-primitive, non-linear, dynamic. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: `[40, 10, 30]`, then `[40, 25, 10, 30]`, then `[25, 10, 30]`, then `[25, 10, 99]`, then `[10, 25, 99]`. After the delete the structure has three items, so index 2 is the last one. (5 marks)

questions.title: Question 2: Strings, loops and files (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) For `String dept = "Computer Science";` give `dept.length() * 10`, `dept.indexOf("scie")`, `dept.substring(9) + 7` and say what `dept.charAt(dept.length())` does. (b) Give the value of `sum` for `for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i += 2) sum += i;` and name the loop error. (c) Explain why a file written with `PrintWriter` may be empty and give the two ways to handle `FileNotFoundException`. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: 160; -1 (the search is case-sensitive and the text has a capital S); `Science7`; `charAt(length())` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` because the valid indexes are 0 to 15. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `i` takes 1, 3, 5, so `sum` is 9. The error is an incorrect update (`i += 2` instead of `i++`). (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: The `PrintWriter` keeps the text in a buffer; `close()` writes it, so a file that is not closed may be empty. `FileNotFoundException` is handled with a `throws` clause on the method or a `try-catch` block; otherwise the compiler reports `unreported exception FileNotFoundException`. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** 160, -1, `Science7`, an exception; 9; close the file and handle the exception.

questions.title: Question 3: Parameters, returns and scope (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) Why does `total = 10; t = addTax(total, 7.5);` leave `total` at 10.0 when `addTax` sets `price = price + tax`? (b) What does `javac` report for a `sign(double x)` method with no return for `x == 0`? (c) Why does a variable declared in a `for` block fail when printed after the loop, and what does `javac` report? (d) With a static `count = 3`, a method `addOne(int count)` and a later local `int count = 50` in `main`, what are the outputs of `addOne(count)` and of `count` and `ScopeTrace.count` after the declaration? (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: A copy of the value is passed; the method changes its own copy `price`, not the original in the calling method. Return the new value and assign it. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `error: missing return statement`: the compiler complains if any branch has no return. Make sure all conditions are handled. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: A block variable stops existing at the closing brace; the compiler reports `error: cannot find symbol`. Declare it before the block if it is needed afterwards. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (d)
steps.body: `addOne(count)` receives a copy of the global 3 and returns 4, and the global is unchanged (`4 3`). After `int count = 50;` the name means the local variable: `50`, and the global is reached as `ScopeTrace.count`, still 3. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** `10.0`; `missing return statement`; `cannot find symbol`; `4 3` then `50 3`.

questions.title: Question 4: The range reader (10 marks)
questions.prompt: The lecture's `readValueBetween(low, high)` starts with `int input = 0;` and loops `while (input < low || input > high)`. (a) What does it do for the range 1 to 12 when the user types 20, -3 and 8? (b) What does it do for the range 0 to 59, and why? (c) Give the repair. (10 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: It asks three times: 20 and -3 are outside the range and are rejected, 8 is accepted and returned. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: It returns 0 without asking anything: the starting value 0 is already inside 0 to 59, so the loop condition is false at once and no input is read. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: Start with a value that is certainly outside the range, `int input = low - 1;`, or use a `do-while` loop, which always runs once. With the repair the minutes range rejects 75 and accepts 30. (3 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** The unrepaired method returns 0 for the minutes without asking; start with `low - 1`.

questions.title: Question 5: Arrays and memory (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) Give the contents of `numbers` after `numbers[0] = 5; for (int i = 1; i < numbers.length; i++) { numbers[i] = i * i + 5; if (i > 2) { numbers[i] = 2 * numbers[i] - numbers[i - 1]; } }` for `new int[6]`. (b) For `int n = 10; int[] numbers = new int[n + 4];` and a loop that sets `numbers[i] = i + 1` when `i` is odd, state the output of the loop and of `numbers.length`. (c) Why does a method `initArray` change the caller's array while `arr = new int[]{7, 7, 7}` inside a method does not? (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: Work one value of `i` at a time, using the new value of the previous cell: i = 1: 6; i = 2: 9; i = 3: 14, then 28 - 9 = 19; i = 4: 21, then 42 - 19 = 23; i = 5: 30, then 60 - 23 = 37. The contents are `5, 6, 9, 19, 23, 37`. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: The array has 14 cells and only the odd indexes are written, so it prints 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (one per line) and then 14. (3 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: The parameter is a copy of the address. Changing an element follows the address and changes the caller's array; assigning a new array moves only the parameter, so the caller's variable still holds the old address. (4 marks)

questions.title: Question 6: Arrays of objects and array methods (12 marks)
questions.prompt: (a) For `Account[] accs = new Account[5]; accs[0] = new Account(190, 450.0);` say what happens for `accs[0].equals(accs[3])` and for `printf("%d", accs[0].getBalance())`, and how each is repaired. (b) Write `countAbove(int[] numbers, double limit)` and `indexOfMin(int[] numbers)`, and give their results for `{3, 1, -2, 6, 8}` with the average as the limit. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: `accs[3]` was never assigned, so `equals` receives `null` and fails with `NullPointerException`: assign an account first or test for `null`. `%d` expects an integer and the balance is a `double`, so it throws `IllegalFormatConversionException`: use `%.2f`. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `countAbove` loops over the elements and counts those greater than `limit`; `indexOfMin` assumes index 0 and replaces it when a smaller element is found. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: The average is 16 / 5 = 3.2, the elements above it are 6 and 8 so `countAbove` returns 2, and the smallest element is -2 so `indexOfMin` returns 2. (3 marks)

questions.title: Question 7: Labs 1 and 2 (14 marks)
questions.prompt: In Lab 1 each record is `number;customer ID;total;paid`. (a) Give the outstanding amount of lay-byes with (total, paid) of (1000, 400), (800, 400), (2000, 0) and (500, 500), and say which go to `concern.txt`. (b) In Lab 2, for the records (4000, 1000), (5000, 5000), (5001, 0), (-50, 0) and (2000, 2500), say which are removed by `preProcessing` and which by `validate`. (c) What does `linearSearch` return, and relative to which array? (14 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: The outstanding amounts are 600, 400, 2000 and 0. The concern file holds those whose outstanding amount **exceeds** half the total: (1000, 400) since 600 > 500, and (2000, 0) since 2000 > 1000. (800, 400) owes exactly half, which does not exceed it, and (500, 500) is paid up. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: `preProcessing` removes (5001, 0), whose total exceeds P5000, and (-50, 0), whose total is negative. `validate` removes (2000, 2500), whose paid amount exceeds its total. (4000, 1000) and (5000, 5000) are kept: 5000 does not exceed P5000 and a paid amount equal to the total is not an error. (5 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: `linearSearch` compares each element in turn and returns the index of the item with the ID, or -1 when it is not found. The index is a position in the array that was given, here the array of valid items. (4 marks)
